title: Why Is Mary Called Blessed Among Women?
paragraphs:
Why Is Mary Called Blessed Among Women?
The Scandal, the Surrender, and the Grace That Changed Human History Forever
There are moments in history so sacred that heaven seems to hold its breath.
This is one of them.
A young woman. No throne. No wealth. No political influence. No army. No status that the world would admire.
Just a teenage girl from Nazareth.
And yet her name would be spoken for thousands of years.
Not because she was powerful.
Not because she was perfect.
Not because she was divine.
But because she said yes when obedience carried a price.
Many people know Mary.
Few truly understand why Scripture calls her blessed among women.
The answer is far deeper than most imagine.
It begins with a scandal.
Before there was a manger, there was suspicion.
Before there was worship, there were whispers.
Before there was Christmas, there was a young woman carrying a miracle that looked like a disgrace.
Imagine hearing the rumors.
Imagine seeing the judgment in people's eyes.
Imagine trying to explain what even you barely understood.
The Gospel of Luke records the angel's astonishing greeting:
"Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ Κύριος μετὰ σοῦ."
(Luke 1:28)
A careful translation from the Greek reads:
"Greetings, favored one, the Lord is with you."
The word "κεχαριτωμένη" (kecharitōmenē) carries the idea of one who has received grace and favor from God.
Mary was not blessed because she earned grace.
Mary was blessed because she received grace.
That distinction matters.
The Bible never presents Mary as the source of grace.
It presents her as a recipient of grace.
God chose her.
God favored her.
God entrusted her with a mission unlike any other in human history.
Then came words that would forever change the world.
"Behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus."
Luke 1:31
The Son she would carry was not merely a prophet.
Not merely a teacher.
Not merely a revolutionary.
He was the promised Messiah.
The Savior.
The Lamb of God.
The eternal Word who became flesh.
The One foretold centuries earlier.
The One who would crush the serpent's head.
The One who would bear humanity's sin upon Himself.
Mary's response reveals why she is called blessed.
She did not fully understand.
She did not know how people would react.
She did not know the pain that awaited her.
She did not know she would one day watch nails driven into the hands she once held as a baby.
She simply answered:
"Ἰδοὺ ἡ δούλη Κυρίου· γένοιτό μοι κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου."
(Luke 1:38)
"Behold, I am the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word."
That is the language of surrender.
That is the language of faith.
That is the language of someone willing to lose everything if it means obeying God.
Most people want blessing without surrender.
Mary teaches us that God's greatest blessings often arrive wrapped inside costly obedience.
Shortly afterward, Mary visited Elizabeth.
The moment Mary arrived, something extraordinary happened.
Luke records:
"Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤκουσεν ἡ Ἐλισάβετ τὸν ἀσπασμὸν τῆς Μαρίας, ἐσκίρτησεν τὸ βρέφος."
The baby in Elizabeth's womb leaped.
Then Elizabeth cried out:
"Εὐλογημένη σὺ ἐν γυναιξίν."
(Luke 1:42)
"Blessed are you among women."
This is the phrase that has echoed through history.
Notice what Elizabeth did not say.
She did not say Mary was above women.
She did not say Mary was a goddess.
She did not say Mary was equal to God.
She declared that among women, Mary was uniquely blessed because God had chosen her for a unique role in His redemptive plan.
The blessing was connected to God's purpose.
Not personal greatness.
Even Mary herself understood this.
Her famous song, often called the Magnificat, begins:
"Μεγαλύνει ἡ ψυχή μου τὸν Κύριον."
(Luke 1:46)
"My soul magnifies the Lord."
Notice where Mary's attention goes.
Not toward herself.
Toward God.
True biblical honor always points back to the Lord.
Mary's life never says, "Look at me."
Mary's life says, "Look at Him."
That is why she remains one of the most beautiful examples of faith in all Scripture.
Yet her story is also deeply personal.
Because most of us know what it feels like to carry something people misunderstand.
A calling.
A burden.
A season of suffering.
A decision to obey God that others question.
A chapter where faith looks foolish.
Mary reminds us that God's work in our lives is often misunderstood before it is celebrated.
The same crowd that eventually celebrated Jesus would have initially questioned His mother's story.
God's plans frequently pass through seasons that appear scandalous before they reveal their glory.
That truth reaches its ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Himself.
Think about it.
Born in humble circumstances.
Rejected by many.
Mocked.
Accused.
Beaten.
Crucified.
Everything about the cross looked like failure.
Everything about the cross looked like scandal.
Yet three days later the greatest reversal in history occurred.
The empty tomb transformed apparent defeat into eternal victory.
That is the Gospel.
That is why our message is "From Scandal to Grace."
Because Jesus rewrites everything.
The broken become restored.
The guilty become forgiven.
The lost become found.
The ashamed become redeemed.
The sinner becomes a child of God.
Mary's story ultimately points beyond Mary.
It points to Christ.
Every blessing she received came through Him.
Every prophecy centered on Him.
Every act of obedience served Him.
Every road in her life led to Him.
And every road in Scripture leads there too.
Perhaps that is why this story still grips hearts today.
Because deep down we all hope God can rewrite our story.
We know our failures.
We remember our regrets.
We carry wounds no one sees.
We remember nights we cried ourselves to sleep.
Moments we wanted to quit.
Chapters we wish could be erased.
The Gospel declares that Jesus specializes in rewriting stories that seem beyond repair.
If He could bring redemption through a manger and victory through a cross, He can bring hope into your situation too.
No scandal is greater than His grace.
No failure is stronger than His mercy.
No darkness can extinguish His light.
No sinner is beyond His reach.
Maybe that is the real reason Mary's story endures.
Not because it exalts a human being.
But because it reveals what God can do through someone who trusts Him.
And maybe today that invitation is for you.
Not to become Mary.
But to have Mary's faith.
The faith that says:
"I do not understand everything."
"I do not know what comes next."
"But Lord, I trust You."
Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs today.
Sometimes it becomes part of someone's salvation story.
One share.
One article.
One testimony.
One soul pointed toward Christ.
And eternity remembers what the world forgets.
The same God who chose an unknown girl from Nazareth is still transforming ordinary lives through extraordinary grace.
Long after the rumors faded, the grace remained.
